papers.whyItMatters: Gravity dual. E-HOL stays cut from the engine.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: On the (In)equivalence of de Sitter and Holographic Entanglement Entropies in Lovelock Gravity
papers.coreIdea: Compares de Sitter entropy with holographic entanglement entropy in higher-curvature gravity.
papers.whyItMatters: No code, no plasma, no ledger term. Denylist.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Where's Kasner? OPE Signature of Kasner Exponents
papers.coreIdea: Large-N thermal correlators are used as a signature of Kasner exponents near a holographic black-hole singularity.
papers.whyItMatters: Reading for holography. Not an INCLUDE. The denylist does not move.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Blast freezing a black hole
papers.coreIdea: A solvable evaporation model built from coupled Sachdev–Ye–Kitaev systems, in which a black hole is suddenly coupled to a colder bath.
papers.whyItMatters: The word Kitaev here is a random-matrix model, not a braid. SYK evaporation is E-HOL reading.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Amplified Memory and Finite-Time Regularity in Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.coreIdea: Driving a non-Hermitian Kitaev chain through a broken-spectrum region amplifies the memory of how the state was prepared, for a finite time.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC is cut as a clock. A transient memory in a non-Hermitian chain is not a metronome and not a Majorana logical qubit.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dirac condensate in bosonic Kitaev chain
papers.coreIdea: A mean-field Bose condensate on a bosonic Kitaev chain forms a staggered phase once pairing is strong enough.
papers.whyItMatters: Bosons, not fermion zero modes. Does not touch E-MZM's logical-qubit test.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: GIMLI: a toolkit connecting linear and non-linear magnetohydrodynamic regimes
papers.coreIdea: A bridge that seeds the nonlinear MHD code MPI-AMRVAC with linear modes from Legolas. One example is an interchange mode in a straight tokamak; the others are solar and astrophysical.
papers.whyItMatters: A unit-test tokamak is not a disruption metric and not a coil API. E-RL is not moved.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: The quadratic density response function for non-interacting fermions at arbitrary temperature
papers.coreIdea: The quadratic density response of non-interacting fermions, with a classical limit taken from the Vlasov equation. Aimed at warm dense matter.
papers.whyItMatters: Vlasov appears as a warm-dense-matter limit, not as hole-burning or a fusion reactivity. S-L3 is not moved.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Monte Carlo sampling of first-order QED processes in laser and pulsar plasmas
papers.coreIdea: A sampling scheme for strong-field QED event rates in intense lasers and pulsar magnetospheres.
papers.whyItMatters: Pair-production sampling is not laser-assisted DT tunneling. It does not beat the PRC 109 field bound and does not enter the ledger.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Eigenoperator Entanglement Statistics in Local Lindbladians
papers.coreIdea: Asks whether chaotic open quantum systems have eigenoperators that look Haar-random, using entanglement of Liouvillian eigenoperators.
papers.whyItMatters: Lindblad here is a chaos diagnostic, not a plasma coherence penalty P_coh(n,T). S-L1 is not moved.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Quantum Trajectories
papers.coreIdea: A variational ansatz of superposed Gaussian packets for stochastic trajectories unraveled from a bosonic master equation.
papers.whyItMatters: An open-system solver for bosons. Not a fusion density matrix and not a code threshold.
papers.limitation: Off-path. Not in the paper.

papers.title: Decoder Model Compatibility Provides Information beyond the Logical Gap under Drifting and Correlated Quantum Noise
papers.coreIdea: When a quantum chip drifts, the decoder's noise model goes stale, and shots that look surprising under that stale model are the ones most likely to be wrong. Throwing those shots out, using a weight the decoder already computes, cuts the logical errors you keep: about 11% and 29% on IBM repetition-code memories (distance 7 and 9, discarding 15% of shots), and about 75% on a published Google distance-5 surface-code memory if you discard 90%.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer on Bus B, and this reuses Google's own surface-code memory data plus IBM hardware. It is a postselection filter on logical error, not a new code, not an S3 fusion gate, and not a plant controller.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. The headline Google drop throws away nine shots in ten. It does not move the surface-code threshold and it is not a term in the Q ledger, so it cannot raise C4.

papers.title: Bosonic Error Correction with Fluxonium
papers.coreIdea: A heavy fluxonium qubit, whose bit flips last about 450 microseconds, controls a tiny on-chip microwave resonator and holds a GKP grid state using measurement-free correction. The logical lifetime is about 1.6 times longer than without that correction. It is the first standalone bosonic error correction in a fully planar superconducting circuit.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC cares that error correction runs on hardware labs already build. This is a real device result on a superconducting chip. It is a bosonic grid code, not the surface-code or qLDPC layer that carries the C4.
papers.limitation: One device, one factor of 1.59, bare arXiv. No distance scaling and no surface-code threshold. Cannot raise C4 and does not enter the energy ledger.

papers.title: AI-Accelerated Gyrokinetic Predictions of Turbulent Transport for Stellarator Design Optimization and Experimental Planning
papers.coreIdea: A neural stand-in for a nonlinear gyrokinetic code predicts turbulent ion heat flux in milliseconds instead of a full simulation. Trained on more than 200,000 runs across about 23,000 stellarator shapes, it lets a designer optimize the magnetic equilibrium directly against that heat flux and then check the resulting ion temperature in a transport solver.
papers.whyItMatters: This sits on both Bus A and Bus C and therefore couples them. E-RL wants a module that can attach to a machine; S-L3 wants the kinetic solver kept honest. A millisecond surrogate is a design tool. It does not command coils during a shot and it does not write a plant Q.
papers.limitation: Offline optimization of a stellarator equilibrium, not a closed disruption loop and not a driven-barrier rate. Two claims means the coupling starts at C1. Neither E-RL nor S-L3 moves.

papers.title: Error Suppression in Distributed Quantum Computing with Heterogeneous-Distance Lattice Surgery
papers.coreIdea: When two quantum processors are linked by a noisy connection, you do not have to enlarge every code patch. This layout enlarges only the ancilla that straddles the link and keeps the data patches at distance d. In circuit-level simulations of rotated surface codes, the logical readout error depends only weakly on how noisy that link is, and the qubit count stays below a uniform larger code.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC on Bus B will eventually be modular. A surgery schedule that confines link noise is a compile-time option for surface-code patches. It is not an anyon braid and not a tokamak actuator.
papers.limitation: Depolarizing-noise simulation, not a device. No measured threshold. Bare arXiv, so C4 stays where Google's surface-code experiment put it.

papers.title: Electronic Reconstruction Towards Topological Superconductivity in FeTe
papers.coreIdea: Annealing excess iron out of a 20-layer FeTe film turns an antiferromagnetic metal into a superconductor. Photoemission shows the bands rearrange, including a topological surface state, and the authors say that combination is a place to look for Majorana bound states.
papers.whyItMatters: E-MZM is the watch item for M5. A real superconducting film with a topological surface state is a materials candidate. It is not a parity readout, not a braid, and not an X or Z logical qubit.
papers.limitation: No zero-bias peak, no gap scaling, no logical operation. The Majorana sentence is a prospect, not a measurement. WATCH stays C1. A1 fails because E-MZM is not KEEP or HOLD.

papers.title: Reduction technique for expanding the Feynman diagrams in AdS2
papers.coreIdea: A bookkeeping method that rewrites tree-level Feynman diagrams in two-dimensional anti-de Sitter space as networks of Wilson lines, checked on five-point diagrams.
papers.whyItMatters: It is an AdS calculation. E-HOL is cut as a reactor or processor part. Reading is allowed. It does not sit on a bus.
papers.limitation: Denylist. No interface, no plasma, no code threshold. Cannot INCLUDE.

papers.title: A Majorana Formulation of Time-Dependent Two-Particle Reduced-Density-Matrix Dynamics
papers.coreIdea: A numerical trick that writes interacting fermions as Majorana operators so a two-particle density matrix can be stepped in time. It is tested on a Hubbard quench and on flux motion in the Kitaev honeycomb model.
papers.whyItMatters: The word Majorana here is the fermion algebra, not a zero-mode qubit. It does not test E-MZM and must not be read as a braid or a logical gate.
papers.limitation: Keyword collision. Off-path. Not a distinguisher for M5.

papers.title: Sipser-Spielman meets Dijkgraaf-Witten: non-Abelian qLDPC codes via twisted sheaf gauge theory and almost-constant-overhead magic state fountain
papers.coreIdea: A new family of quantum error-correcting codes is built by twisting a classical expander code with a non-Abelian D4 gauge theory. The same construction is used as a magic-state fountain: it prepares many CZ magic states at once, and with a newer algebraic code the number of those states grows almost in step with the number of qubits.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer on Bus B, and this is a qLDPC construction whose topological order is non-Abelian D4. It does not replace E-S3. The cyclic-fusion test that makes S3 universal excludes D4, so braid-plus-fusion on S3 stays the topological primitive.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No device and no measured threshold. The almost-constant magic rate still gives up distance as the slack parameter goes to zero. It is not a term in the Q ledger and cannot raise C4.

papers.title: Demonstration of H-mode Error Field Identification in a Single Discharge via Island Healing
papers.coreIdea: On KSTAR, the plasma control system finds the magnetic error field that opens a tearing island during a single H-mode pulse, by healing the island while the coils scan. Older compass scans on DIII-D, JET, and MAST-U needed several discharges and were not done in H-mode. Cutting the scan from four shots to one is up to a 75% reduction in the time that calibration costs.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL is the plant-attach claim. This is a real tokamak control system doing error-field identification in H-mode, the regime a pilot plant has to live in. It is a classical coil procedure. No quantum hardware is in the loop.
papers.limitation: One machine, bare arXiv. It shortens a calibration scan. It does not beat a lab baseline on disruption rate or tearing-onset warning, so M2 stays open. The 75% is not an energy-ledger term and cannot raise C4.

papers.title: Impact of magnetic drift configuration on the edge radial electric field in the TCV tokamak
papers.coreIdea: On TCV, Doppler backscattering shows a well in the edge radial electric field just inside the separatrix when the ion drift points the favorable way, and a weaker or missing well when the drift is reversed. The difference is still there when edge density and temperature match, and it sharpens as the plasma is heated toward H-mode.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL's attach surface includes TCV. This is a measured edge-field fact a shape or L-H controller would have to respect. The paper does not send a coil command.
papers.limitation: Diagnostic only. No actuator, no latency budget, and no disruption metric. Bare arXiv. It cannot close M2 and cannot raise C4.

papers.title: Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill error-correction with decohered resources
papers.coreIdea: Standard GKP error correction assumes a perfectly quiet ancilla pair. If that ancilla is only allowed to dephase, teleportation no longer snaps the state back into the code. The correction becomes a noise process that piles up, and after a few rounds the leakage out of the code saturates instead of healing.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC needs to know when a bosonic code stops correcting itself. A dephased GKP ancilla does not self-correct. The default error layer is still the surface code and qLDPC, not GKP.
papers.limitation: Theory of one noise channel on GKP. No device, no distance scaling, and no surface-code threshold. Bare arXiv. It does not lower C4 and it writes no ledger term.

papers.title: Measurement-Based Uncomputation from an Error Correction Perspective
papers.coreIdea: Uncomputing scratch qubits can cost as much as the computation itself. Measuring the scratch register and keeping only the no-error outcomes throws the garbage away without running the reverse circuit. The success rate is set by how the garbage is populated, which can be much smaller than the number of garbage qubits. Other outcomes can be fixed by reusing the original uncompute only when a structural condition holds.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC cares about spacetime overhead on early fault-tolerant machines. This is a postselection rule on the garbage register, not a new code and not a measured threshold.
papers.limitation: The cheap version discards shots. The worked example is HHL, not a surface-code memory. Bare arXiv. No measured logical error and no Q term.

papers.title: Bootstrapping Holographic Theories in the Planar Limit
papers.coreIdea: A numerical bootstrap combined with localization puts an upper bound on the lightest single-trace operator in two holographic gauge theories, at every value of the coupling. Where integrability is known, the bound sits close to it.
papers.whyItMatters: It is a holographic spectrum bound. E-HOL is cut as a reactor or processor part. Reading is allowed. It does not sit on a bus.
papers.limitation: Denylist. No plasma, no code threshold, no interface. Cannot INCLUDE.

papers.title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. I. Massive particles
papers.coreIdea: Sending the radius of anti-de Sitter space to infinity turns conformal representations into the Hilbert space of ordinary massive particles, and the inner product stays unitary through that limit.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the flat-space limit of AdS/CFT. E-HOL is cut. It does not encode a plasma state or a logical qubit.
papers.limitation: Denylist. No bus, no energy accounting. Cannot INCLUDE.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Non-Hermitian Skin Effect with Floquet-Engineered Ultracold Atoms
papers.coreIdea: Ultracold atoms driven in a repeating pattern show a non-Hermitian skin effect: bulk states pile up at the edge. The drive is Floquet. The result is about where the wavefunction sits, not about keeping time.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC as a system clock is cut. A Floquet skin effect in a cold-atom lattice is many-body physics. It does not tick a control cycle or a QEC round.
papers.limitation: Not a metronome. No comparison to a QEC-cycle lifetime. Cannot INCLUDE.

papers.title: Generation of Photonic Graph States with minimal number of quantum emitters
papers.coreIdea: Photonic graph states can be built with fewer quantum emitters if the order the photons are emitted is chosen carefully. The paper's fusion is the photonic operation that glues graph states together. It is not a measurement of non-Abelian anyons.
papers.whyItMatters: The word fusion is a false friend for E-S3. Graph-state fusion does not braid S3 fluxes and does not read their fusion space. It is also not a plasma rate.
papers.limitation: About a 30% emitter cut on random graphs, from a heuristic. No anyon, no plant, no energy ledger. Off-path.

papers.title: Observer-Based Model Predictive Control for Isoflux Regulation in the EXL-50U Spherical Tokamak
papers.coreIdea: A model-predictive controller for the EXL-50U spherical tokamak is asked to hold plasma current and the plasma boundary at the same time, with coil voltage limits written in. On a computer model of the machine it tracks those targets more tightly than a standard PID loop or a linear-quadratic regulator, and the sum is done in under a millisecond.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL is the plant-attach claim. This is the right kind of machine and the right kind of job: shape and current, coils, a latency number. It is still a simulation of EXL-50U, not a shot. It does not beat a lab baseline on disruptions, so M2 stays open.
papers.limitation: No plasma was controlled. The paper says the runs are a basis for future experiments. The error numbers (1.126 kA, 0.0164 m, 2.463 mWb) are against PID inside a Grad–Shafranov model. They are not a Q term and cannot raise C4.

papers.title: A packet-level digital hardware twin for commissioning megahertz diagnostic edge AI and plasma control system integration in tokamaks
papers.coreIdea: Fast cameras and beam-emission diagnostics are too quick to bolt onto a plasma control system by hand. This paper builds a packet-level twin of that path: a 64-channel, 1 MHz diagnostic, dropped packets, and a 1 kHz control cycle. A missing packet is caught and the bad windows are thrown out instead of being filled in.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL needs a latency budget and a safe-hold when data is lost. The twin measures a median handoff of 91.6 microseconds into shared memory. That is the diagnostic side of Bus A. It never moved a coil on a plasma.
papers.limitation: Commissioning simulator, not a tokamak shot. 91.6 µs is last-input to shared memory, not actuator-to-plasma. A 1 kHz cycle can still be slower than a tearing mode. No disruption metric, so M2 stays open. Not a Q term.

papers.title: A Rapid Integrated Tokamak Modelling Approach for Coupled Profile and Equilibrium Evolution
papers.coreIdea: During a current ramp the plasma's heat and its magnetic field change on different clocks. This paper ties a fixed-boundary equilibrium to a fast particle-and-energy balance and to current diffusion, and runs an ITER-like deuterium pulse (10 to 15 MA, 80 MW of electron-cyclotron heating) in seconds on a laptop.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL's offline twin has to be fast enough to sit next to a controller. The stored-energy check against an independent code (FUSE) is 0.02 percent at 60 s. That is a solver benchmark. It is not a coil command and it is not a plant gain.
papers.limitation: Fixed boundary, pure deuterium, one scenario. The largest disagreement with FUSE is the core current, which is what a controller would care about. Stored energy 185.52 to 252.70 MJ is a model output under a prescribed 80 MW, not Q_eng. M2 stays open.

papers.title: Positivity-preserving semi-Lagrangian discontinuous Galerkin methods for multi-species Vlasov-Ampère models of plasma
papers.coreIdea: A kinetic plasma code has to keep the particle distribution from going negative when ions and electrons live on very different scales. This paper builds a high-order Vlasov–Ampère solver that enforces that positivity, and checks it on standard waves: Landau damping, two-stream instability, and KEEN waves.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 says the Vlasov piece must sit in any fusion-rate claim. A positivity-preserving multi-species solver is a method the ledger is allowed to use later. It does not contain hole-burning, SRS, or SBS, and it does not report a reactivity.
papers.limitation: Test problems only. No fusion cross-section, no drive laser, no auxiliary power. Keeping the distribution positive is not a gain. C4 on S-L3 stays where it was; this does not move it.

papers.title: Ion-temperature-gradient turbulence from finite to weak magnetic shear regime
papers.coreIdea: Hot tokamak plasma leaks heat because of a turbulence called the ion temperature gradient. This paper says that when the magnetic shear gets weaker than about 1 over 2π, that turbulence changes shape and, in their simulations, an internal barrier forms and the turbulence drops inside that region.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 is the kinetic transport layer the rate is not allowed to ignore. A geometric criterion checked on DIII-D, JET, and ITER parameters is a transport result. It is not a reactivity ratio and it is not a control attach.
papers.limitation: Gyrokinetic simulations, not a shot. Real internal barriers have more than one cause. The paper does not compute fusion power, drive power, or Q. A confinement story must not be copied into the ledger as a gain.

papers.title: Implicit-Explicit time integration scheme with Physics-based preconditioning for two-fluid tokamak boundary simulations
papers.coreIdea: The edge of a tokamak is stiff: Alfvén waves want a tiny time step. This paper puts those fast pieces in an implicit solver inside the GBS boundary code and leaves the slower pieces explicit, so the step can be longer without paying for a fully implicit run.
papers.whyItMatters: Boundary turbulence is part of the loss stack next to S-L3. A faster GBS step is a method improvement. It is not a Vlasov solver and it is not a fusion rate.
papers.limitation: Two-fluid, not kinetic. Manufactured-solution checks. No hole-burning, no SRS/SBS, no Q. A bigger time step is not a gain.

papers.title: Circuit-level benchmarks of GKP-concatenated qLDPC Codes
papers.coreIdea: A GKP code stores a qubit in a harmonic oscillator and can pass analog clues to the decoder. This paper wraps two qLDPC families (BB and tricycle) around that inner code and simulates noisy circuits. Using the analog clue raises the noise level the code can stand, on paper, and the BB family needs less squeezing than the tricycle family in their setup.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer on Bus B. A circuit-level comparison of qLDPC outer codes is in the right literature. It is a simulation of a bosonic stack, not a measured surface-code threshold, and it is not an S3 gate.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. Finite-size crossings under shared assumptions: about 0.212 and 0.142, quoted as 10.46 dB and 13.94 dB of squeezing. No device. Does not move the Google surface-code result that holds C4.

papers.title: Disentangling the Toric Code
papers.coreIdea: The toric code can be thought of as a symmetry that is not a simple on-site spin flip, because its excitations are anyons. The paper proves that no finite extra quantum system can turn that symmetry into an on-site one. Infinite-dimensional extras can, but only if their energy is not bounded from below.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC's memory is the toric code and its surface-code descendants. A proof that finite ancillas cannot erase the anyons is a structural fact about that memory. It is not a threshold, not a decoder, and not the S3 fusion gate.
papers.limitation: Theorem, not a device. The infinite-ancilla loophole needs an unbounded Hamiltonian, so it is not a hardware recipe. Abelian toric-code order does not make S3 universal. C4 is untouched.

papers.title: Read-Rezayi fractional Chern insulators in modulated Bernal graphene
papers.coreIdea: Fibonacci anyons can, in theory, do universal quantum computing by braiding alone. They show up in a fractional quantum Hall state called Read-Rezayi. This paper searches a model of modulated bilayer graphene at zero magnetic field and finds a parameter region whose ground state looks like that state, plus a Moore-Read-like state at another filling.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 is universal only because fusion measurement is kept. Fibonacci braid-only universality is a different route. A numerical ground state in a graphene model does not replace the S3 primitive that has already run on trapped ions, and it does not open a new bus.
papers.limitation: Band-projected exact diagonalization. 'Consistent with' is not a braid and not a fusion measurement. No device. Zero-field non-Abelian order in graphene remains a hypothesis. C3 on E-S3 stays on the Quantinuum result.

papers.title: Extracting the anyonic exchange phase from co-tunneling through an open quantum dot
papers.coreIdea: Abelian anyons in a fractional quantum Hall fluid pick up a phase when they trade places. The paper designs a small interferometer where an open quantum dot makes that swap show up as a shift between two interference patterns, and writes a formula for the current at finite temperature.
papers.whyItMatters: Readout of an anyon is part of topological computing. This proposal is for Laughlin quasiparticles, which are Abelian. E-S3 needs the fusion space of non-Abelian S3 fluxes. An Abelian phase plateau does not provide that space.
papers.limitation: Keldysh calculation, not a device. The exchange phase is θ=πν for Laughlin states. Screening of the area, or a two-drain subtraction, has to be good to a few percent. No non-Abelian braid. Cannot raise C3.

papers.title: Kitaev-Heisenberg model on the square-hexagon-dodecagon lattice
papers.coreIdea: A Kitaev magnet can be rewritten with Majorana fermions moving in a gauge field. On this lattice the pure Kitaev model is gapped almost everywhere, and that gapped phase is a toric code. Which plaquette carries which Abelian anyon depends on the couplings. Adding Heisenberg exchange produces ordinary magnetic order.
papers.whyItMatters: E-MZM is the watch item for Majorana qubits. This is a spin-liquid calculation whose topological phase is Abelian. It does not show a non-Abelian logical qubit, and it does not pass the M5 test.
papers.limitation: Lattice model. The anyons are e and m of a toric code, assigned by fermion parity of vortices. No wire, no gap scaling, no X and Z logicals. E-MZM stays at C1 and is not load-bearing.

papers.title: Continuous Laser-Driven α Source
papers.coreIdea: A laser knocks protons out of a thin water jet, and those protons hit boron nitride and make alpha particles from proton-boron fusion. Because the water keeps flowing, they fired 18,000 shots at 10 hertz without replacing a solid target.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L2 is Floquet-assisted tunneling of DT at extreme fields. This experiment is a laser-driven proton-boron source for alphas. It is not a driven Coulomb barrier, it quotes no electric field, and it is not a reactor gain.
papers.limitation: Target-normal sheath acceleration into a converter. Yield is benchmarked against particle transport, not against a thermal DT rate. No P_drive in the ledger, no Q. Eighteen thousand shots do not move the 10^15 V/m bound.

papers.title: Interactions Protect Periodically Driven Time Crystals Against Dephasing but Destabilise Multipolar-Driven Order
papers.coreIdea: In a small kicked spin chain, turning up the interactions helps a periodically driven time crystal survive dephasing. The same interactions hurt the order when the drive is a more irregular multipolar sequence. The chains have 12 or 16 spins.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC as a system clock is already cut. A 16-spin diagonalization does not outlast a QEC cycle and does not time a plasma shot. The physics can be read. It is not timing infrastructure.
papers.limitation: Exact diagonalization at N≤16. Coherence time scales as about 1 over the dephasing rate for the periodic drive. No comparison to a control horizon. Not a metronome.

papers.title: Holography for integrable field theories
papers.coreIdea: Some integrable field theories have a holographic twin: a topological string whose shape is a spectral curve. The paper describes how that curve changes under the renormalization flow and matches known results up to two loops.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A duality between a spectral curve and a field theory is not a sensor, a coil command, or a processor bus. It stays on the reading list.
papers.limitation: No plasma, no qubit, no energy accounting. Matching a two-loop RG flow does not encode a reactor. Denylist holds.

papers.title: Optimal performance in a chaotic Floquet quantum battery
papers.coreIdea: A handful of qubits, kicked on a schedule and disordered, can store energy and give most of it back. In the very disordered limit the stored energy is predictable and the waste looks small, so the authors say the extractable fraction approaches one.
papers.whyItMatters: A closed spin model with unit extractable fraction is not a fusion gain. S-Q is cut as an output. Ergotropy is not Q_eng. The word efficiency must not enter the ledger.
papers.limitation: Permutation-symmetric qubits plus disorder. No plasma, no Bremsstrahlung, no drive laser, no wall plug. Low signal for this program.

papers.title: Symmetry-permuting entanglers for non-invertible symmetry-protected topological phases
papers.coreIdea: Some one-dimensional phases protected by a non-invertible symmetry cannot be connected by a circuit that respects the symmetry. The paper shows they can still be connected if the circuit is allowed to permute the symmetry, and writes an explicit example for Rep(D8).
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 is a two-dimensional quantum double with fusion measurement. A one-dimensional Rep(D8) entangler is not that gate set. D8 is also outside the cyclic-fusion test that picks S3. The paper is not load-bearing.
papers.limitation: Matrix-product unitary in 1+1D. No anyon braid, no fusion measurement, no processor. Not a new pillar and not a bus.

papers.title: Adaptive decoding of quantum LDPC codes through decoder disagreement
papers.coreIdea: A quantum error-correcting decoder usually runs an expensive search on every syndrome. This paper uses a cheap internal disagreement, the quick guess versus a syndrome-consistent guess, to mark the hard cases. Spending that search on only the riskiest fifth of cases recovers most of the accuracy, and the same flag still predicts trouble on a small memory experiment on Quantinuum's H2 ion trap.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer. A decoder that spends classical time only where it helps is part of running qLDPC on a real processor. One H2 memory run does not show that a larger code has a smaller logical error, so C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. The hardware piece is a Z-memory on H2, not a below-threshold scaling plot. Harvest confidence 78 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. Circuit-distance certificates are not this paper's result.

papers.title: Diffusion prior for KSTAR equilibrium reconstruction under sensor dropout
papers.coreIdea: Magnetic sensors do not fix the plasma current profile, and missing sensors make the gap larger. A diffusion model learns only that current profile and is tied to KSTAR's sensor response. On 37 real shots, with as many as 90 percent of the channels switched off in the analysis, its profile stays closer to the full-sensor fit than the standard LIUQE reconstruction does.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL attaches to a machine that already exists. KSTAR shots and a dropout prior are the diagnostic half of Bus A. They do not send a coil command, and they do not beat a disruption baseline. M2 stays open.
papers.limitation: The dropout is applied after the shot, in software. At low dropout, LIUQE is closer on most shots. The high-dropout error is in the vessel current, not a solved control problem. No actuator. Cannot raise C4.

papers.title: Experimental demonstration of broadband-laser suppression of cross-beam energy transfer
papers.coreIdea: In laser fusion, one beam can hand energy to another and bounce light out of the plasma. At the Kunwu laser, two crossed broadband beams, 0.6 percent bandwidth and up to 550 joules, sent less light back than narrowband beams. In the geometry that separates Brillouin scatter from an ordinary reflection, the Brillouin share fell from 3.75 percent to 0.46 percent.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 says stimulated scatter has to sit in the rate. This is a measured scatter channel, not a Vlasov solver and not a reactivity ratio. Less reflected light is a smaller loss. It is not a fusion gain and it is not Floquet tunneling.
papers.limitation: Two-beam table, not a capsule implosion. Intensity about 2.6 times 10 to the 14 watts per square centimeter, far below the published driven-tunneling intensities. Symmetric scatter is still 4.64 percent. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. No Q_eng.

papers.title: Ultra-high-distance quantum memories from amplified qLDPC codes
papers.coreIdea: A large code distance does not by itself protect a memory, because faults during the parity checks can spread. This paper glues a small quantum code to an amplifier so the certified circuit distance multiplies, and it proves when that product holds. Four rounds turn an 18-qubit seed into a code with 13,320 physical qubits, 64 logical qubits, check weight at most 14, and circuit distance at least 48.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC needs codes whose circuit distance is known, not just the ideal distance. This is a certificate for qLDPC memories. It is not a measured logical error on a processor, so it does not move C4.
papers.limitation: Proof and examples. No device. The seed is Abelian qLDPC, not an S3 fusion space. Not an interface contract for a new pillar.

papers.title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
papers.coreIdea: Particles on a one-dimensional lattice can pick up a fractional phase when they pass through each other. This paper computes how that phase reshapes the spin and charge patterns of a multi-component gas, and how it changes the way the cloud expands after a kick. The phase is a one-dimensional exchange statistic.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 stores information in the fusion space of non-Abelian fluxes in two dimensions, and universality needs a fusion measurement. A one-dimensional Anyon-Hubbard phase does not provide that space and does not replace the fusion gate.
papers.limitation: Optical-lattice theory. No braid of C2 fluxes, no fusion measurement, no processor. The companion spin-chain paper (2609.36555) is the same setting and is left unscored. Cannot raise C3.

papers.title: Active normal-fluid feedback in quantum turbulence from holography
papers.coreIdea: Superfluid turbulence is usually split into two fluids that drag on each other through vortices, with the drag put in by hand. This paper replaces that knob with a holographic gravity model, so the normal fluid and the superfluid push back on each other from the equations. The target experiments are cold atoms, not a tokamak.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A duality for quantum turbulence is not a sensor, a coil command, or a processor bus. The author list says Tusbota in one database spelling and Tsubota in the literature; the physics claim does not change.
papers.limitation: Readable. Not INCLUDE. Wormhole-moduli and compact-object holography in the same listing stay unscored. Denylist holds.

papers.title: Asymptotic Pseudospectra in Dissipative Floquet Quantum Systems: Geometric Structures and Observable Dynamics
papers.coreIdea: In a driven, lossy quantum chain, the usual list of frequencies stops describing how observables move once the chain is large. The paper sorts the almost-spectrum into regions and shows, on two solvable models, that those regions can swap which signal lasts longer.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC as a system clock is already cut. Pseudospectra of a dissipative Floquet chain are not a metronome and do not time a plasma shot. The sentence about quantum-computing observables does not name a gate.
papers.limitation: Two exactly solvable models. No prethermal lifetime compared with a control horizon. Not a CUT reversal.

papers.title: Fault Tolerant Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.coreIdea: A quantum memory is fault tolerant only if the information can still be moved after the gates and the measurements are a little noisy. This paper groups memories into phases by that test. Two- and three-dimensional color codes can sit in one phase. It also shows that a wide family of shallow circuits that only measure point-like syndromes, including ordinary preparation of two-dimensional topological codes and of non-Abelian orders with solvable anyon theories, is not fault tolerant.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 and E-QEC both feel this. S3 is a solvable non-Abelian order. The sentence does not erase the 54-qubit H2 demonstration and it does not drop fusion measurement. It does say a shallow point-like prep is not automatically fault tolerant. The pair is a bridge, so coupling stays at C1. Neither C moves.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. Not a device. Harvest confidence 76 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. The no-go is for point-like syndromes, not for every adaptive circuit.

papers.title: Explicit Capacity-Achieving Quantum LDPC Codes List Decodable in Near-linear Time
papers.coreIdea: Sparse quantum codes, where each check touches only a few qubits, were hard to write down and still decode near the best possible radius. This paper gives an explicit sparse family whose list decoder corrects almost out to the quantum Singleton bound, returns a short list, and runs in time that grows only slightly faster than the length of the code.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer. An explicit qLDPC code with a fast list decoder is a compiler target. It is not a below-threshold memory experiment, so C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No processor. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. The sibling LCL construction (2609.40252) stays unscored.

papers.title: Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation for General Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.coreIdea: Measuring the checks of a sparse quantum code has an ordering rule: wherever an X check and a Z check share qubits, the X interactions must come first an even number of times. This paper searches that ordering on a symmetry-reduced copy of the code and lifts the answer. It does not reach the six-layer lower bound on the published weight-6 IBM bicycle codes, and it does reach the bound on some other sparse codes.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC needs a shallow syndrome circuit or the measurement schedule can dominate the logical error. A schedule on a Tanner graph is not a threshold plot. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. Depth is a circuit count, not a device run. Bivariate-bicycle metachecks (2609.39121) stay unscored.

papers.title: FIREWALL: A surrogate model for the rapid assessment of tokamak wall loading and melting by runaway electrons
papers.coreIdea: A runaway-electron beam during a disruption can melt a small patch of the tokamak wall. Full three-dimensional heat calculations are too slow to scan many shots. FIREWALL keeps a library of how those electrons deposit energy in the metal and then runs a one-dimensional heat calculation on each wall tile, fast enough to screen scenarios and to aim the expensive calculation at tiles that approach melting.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL is the plant-attach claim. A wall-damage screen sits next to Bus A. It does not command a coil and it does not beat a disruption-rate baseline, so M2 stays open. Wall heat is not entered as P_rad and it is not a Q.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No actuator. Melting is a damage flag, not an energy-ledger term.

papers.title: Excitation gap of a blockade structure with Z2 topological order
papers.coreIdea: A grid of atoms that block their neighbors can sit in the same phase as the toric code. Proving that excitations still cost a fixed energy in a huge system is usually out of reach. This paper proves a finite gap for one such blockade model, and says the same argument covers a wider family proposed to host non-Abelian quantum-double phases.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 is the non-Abelian quantum double we run by braiding and by fusion on ions. A gap in a Rydberg Hamiltonian is evidence a phase can exist. It is not a braid, and it is not a fusion measurement. Fusion stays in the gate set. C stays at C3.
papers.limitation: The non-Abelian sentence points at models proposed elsewhere (Büchler et al., Phys. Rev. B 114, 065113, 2026). This paper does not braid them. Bare arXiv.

papers.title: Haah's 3D cubic code thermalizes rapidly
papers.coreIdea: Haah's cubic code was a candidate for a three-dimensional quantum memory that corrects itself, because errors cannot line up into long strings. This paper proves that at every temperature above zero the code forgets its state quickly. It is the first analytic proof of that kind of rapid mixing for a fracton code.
papers.whyItMatters: E-FR is already cut as hardware memory. The proof agrees with the cut. It does not put the cubic code on the bus, and it does not change C. A control bit still does not live on a 3D multi-body Hamiltonian.
papers.limitation: One code. X-cube is not this proof. Not a CUT reversal. Bare arXiv, so C is not moved even downward.

papers.title: Exact analytic solutions of classical time crystals
papers.coreIdea: A classical particle in a parabolic well can be given a kinetic energy that prefers a nonzero speed. The motion is periodic and the speed jumps. The paper writes those orbits in closed form.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC as a system clock is cut. A classical periodic orbit does not time a QEC cycle or a plasma shot.
papers.limitation: No quantum prethermal lifetime and no comparison to a control horizon. Not a CUT reversal.

papers.title: The holographic QCD critical point is sensitive to quark flavors
papers.coreIdea: A holographic model of dense nuclear matter moves its critical endpoint when the mix of quark flavors changes. The first-order transition that appears in neutron-star matter disappears in the mix used for heavy-ion collisions.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A QCD phase diagram is not a tokamak state encoder and not a processor bus. This is the holography representative for the 30 Sep listing. The rest of that cluster stays unscored.
papers.limitation: Readable. Not INCLUDE. Reversing the cut would take two independent C≥4 sources. This is not one of them.

papers.title: Is Your AI Fast Enough to Run a Fusion Reactor?
papers.coreIdea: Models already used to help control the DIII-D tokamak were timed on CPU and GPU backends. Once a network is larger than about five million parameters, a CPU takes tens to thousands of milliseconds. A GPU is much faster. The backend has to be chosen together with the control-cycle budget.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL dies if the loop cannot close inside the instability growth time. This paper measures that budget on the machine Bus A attaches to. It does not command a coil and it does not beat a disruption-rate baseline, so M2 stays open. A quantum job in that same loop is slower than the GPU path already under test. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No new shot. No actuator command. Harvest confidence 76 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. Latency is not entered as P_aux or Q_eng.

papers.title: One-Shot any Code
papers.coreIdea: Any sparse quantum code can be thickened into a code that corrects itself in one shot. Below a fixed noise level, the chance of a logical failure falls exponentially as that thickening grows, even when the measurements are noisy. A code that was already single-shot gets a stronger suppression and keeps a threshold that does not depend on which decoder you started with.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer. A construction that turns any qLDPC code into a single-shot code is a compiler target for Bus B. It is not a below-threshold memory experiment, so C stays at C4. It is not an interface contract for a new non-Abelian pillar.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. The threshold p_RG is not a measured device number. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80, so it is not an ADD.

papers.title: Loss-tolerant distributed lattice surgery using fusion networks
papers.coreIdea: Joining two quantum chips with photons is noisy, because photons get lost and optical operations sometimes fail. This paper builds syndrome checks for lattice surgery on the rotated surface code that tolerate that loss. With no local noise, several of the checks still work when half the interface operations are erased. The word fusion here means joining photons, not fusing anyons.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC needs a way to stitch surface-code patches. A 50% interface-erasure threshold is a compiler number for that stitch. It is not the Google below-threshold plot, so C stays at C4. It does not bind E-S3: photon fusion is not an S3 fusion measurement.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. At local error 10^-3 the paper says local noise hides the interface-distance gain. Harvest confidence 72 is under 80, so it is not an ADD.

papers.title: Transport theory for a generic two-arm co-propagating Majorana interferometer with Majorana fermion and edge vortex tunneling
papers.coreIdea: A pair of Majorana edge modes can be wired as an interferometer. The steady electrical conductance does not show the interference of the edge vortices. At low frequency that interference shows up as an effective capacitance, and that capacitance knows the topological spin of the vortices, as long as the two arms match within a thermal length.
papers.whyItMatters: E-MZM is WATCH. A capacitance that tracks topological spin is a proposed electrical signature. It is not an independent X logical and a Z logical, and it does not show a topological gap scaling. M5 stays open. C stays at C1. Not load-bearing.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv theory. No device. Arm mismatch larger than the thermal length washes the signature out. Not an ADD: E-MZM is not KEEP or HOLD.

papers.title: Anyon Proliferation and Anyon Superconductivity in Higgsing Transitions via Conformal Embeddings
papers.coreIdea: Higgsing a Chern-Simons gauge theory can keep or even enlarge the topological order instead of destroying it. In one family, an Abelian state becomes a non-Abelian one by anyon condensation. For odd N the story is a fermionic Laughlin state turning into a charge-2e anyon superconductor that still carries the same chiral Z_N order.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 is a non-Abelian quantum double, and fusion measurement is why braiding it is universal. This paper is about anyon condensation in a field theory. It does not braid, it does not fuse on a processor, and it does not replace that measurement. C stays at C3. Not a new bus.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. Condensable anyons are proposed by branching rules, not measured. Harvest confidence 68 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. Fusion measurement stays in the gate set.

papers.title: Theory of Equivalent Tokamaks for Characterizing Turbulent Transport in Quasi-symmetric Stellarators
papers.coreIdea: A quasi-symmetric stellarator can be matched to a simpler tokamak when you only ask about slow particle drifts. This paper asks the same question for turbulence. To lowest order the match is a circular tokamak fixed by aspect ratio, twist, and magnetic shear. Gyrokinetic runs of the ion-temperature-gradient mode agree quantitatively for some configurations. Not every stellarator has such a twin once you ask for the next order.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 keeps the kinetic solvers in the rate. An equivalent-tokamak map is a way to check an ITG heat flux against a published tokamak baseline. It is not hole-burning, not SRS or SBS, and it writes no Q_eng. C stays at C4. The ledger does not gain a plant number.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. First-order equivalence is not general. Harvest confidence 70 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. No drive field and no P_aux.

papers.title: A baby universe from a large family: booklet cosmology states and quantum error correction
papers.coreIdea: Several holographic theories can be glued into a booklet. In a heavy limit the middle of the bulk pinches off into a closed baby universe. In a Gaussian toy of three pages, a small code hidden in the middle can be approximately recovered from any two pages.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A recovery sentence about AdS pages is not a surface-code memory and not a tokamak encoder. The denylist holds. It does not raise E-QEC.
papers.limitation: No energy ledger. No device falsifier this year. Not a CUT reversal.

papers.title: Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution
papers.coreIdea: Preparing the ground state of a molecule on a quantum computer can be pre-trained classically. This paper does that pre-training with a compressed circuit whose gates are written as Majorana operators, and it reports chemical accuracy on a ruthenium complex and on acenes up to 60 qubits.
papers.whyItMatters: The word Majorana here is a bookkeeping trick for electrons, not a zero mode. E-MZM does not move. There is no topological gap and no X or Z logical. M5 stays open.
papers.limitation: Chemistry benchmark. Not a topological qubit. Low harvest signal and a false friend.

papers.title: Floquet-Universal Hamiltonian Simulation
papers.coreIdea: A periodically driven quantum system can imitate a system that does not change in time. The paper shows which sets of interactions are enough to imitate any Hamiltonian in their algebra, using only fixed-size interaction strengths and a range of drive frequencies that grows as a power of the system size.
papers.whyItMatters: E-TC as a system clock is cut. A theorem about Floquet simulation is not a tick for a QEC cycle or a plasma shot. It does not go back on the bus.
papers.limitation: No prethermal lifetime and no comparison to a control horizon. Not a CUT reversal.

papers.title: Topological Mixed States: Phases of Matter from Axiomatic Approaches
papers.coreIdea: Ordinary topological order is a story about pure ground states. A real device is mixed: it has leaked into the environment. This paper writes three rules — a patch can be repaired from its boundary, correlations die with distance, and the state looks the same everywhere — and calls two mixed states the same phase when coarse-graining makes both obey the rules. Logical memories fall out of those rules.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC already has a measured surface-code memory below threshold. A journal classification of mixed-state phases does not replace that shot and does not tighten a code threshold. It also does not give S3 a new fusion measurement. C stays at C4. Coupling is not opened.
papers.limitation: Phys. Rev. X, 2 Oct 2026, from a June 2025 preprint. Axioms, not a processor. Harvest confidence 78 is under 80, so it is not an ADD. No ledger number moves.

papers.title: Clifford-hierarchy stabilizer formalism with applications to twisted quantum doubles
papers.coreIdea: Pauli checks cannot name every topological code. This paper lets the checks include diagonal gates from one level of the Clifford hierarchy, which is enough to write many twisted quantum doubles of abelian groups as stabilizer states. Measuring those extra checks can also put a pair of qudit toric codes into a logical magic state.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer. This is a language for abelian twisted doubles and a magic-state trick on qudit toric codes. It is not an S3 fusion measurement and it does not replace the H2 gate set. C stays at C4. Not a new bus.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No device. The magic state is two qudit toric codes, not the three-dimensional fusion space of a C2 pair. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80.

papers.title: Parallel algebraic surgery for qLDPC codes with constant shuttling depth
papers.coreIdea: Atom arrays can move qubits, but a logical measurement on a high-rate code can waste the shot on shuttling. This paper designs the code, the auxiliary measurement, and the move list together so a batch of logical Paulis is read with a shuttling depth that stays constant, provided the code has a cyclic symmetry.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC on reconfigurable atoms is already a hardware class under the error layer. Constant shuttling depth is a compiler result. It is not a measured logical error, so C stays at C4. It is not an S3 interface and not a new pillar.
papers.limitation: Protocol only. No atom-array shot. Bare arXiv. Cyclic symmetry limits which logicals can be named. Harvest confidence 73 is under 80.

papers.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
papers.coreIdea: Trading electric anyons for magnetic anyons in the toric code is a logical Hadamard, and doing it twice should be the identity. The paper proves that no Clifford circuit which preserves locality can do that trade and still square to one. The obstruction is the crossing of an electric string with a magnetic string.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC still uses the toric code as the reference memory. A missing order-two local Clifford for electric-magnetic exchange does not raise the logical error and does not remove the surface code. It is not an S3 fusion gate. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Proof for the Z2 toric code. Bare arXiv. A non-Clifford or a non-local circuit is not forbidden. Harvest confidence 78 is under 80.

papers.title: Transport Impacts of Resonant Island Chains in Fusion Plasmas
papers.coreIdea: Edge transport is often drawn as diffusion through a fully scrambled magnetic layer. On DIII-D discharge 171491, with strong n=3 resonant magnetic perturbations, nested island chains and their invariant manifolds keep field lines from mixing that fast. The scrambled model overestimates the transport.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL attaches to DIII-D. A transport barrier changes what a coil perturbation does to the heat, but this paper does not command a coil and does not beat a disruption rate. M2 stays open. Nothing is written as Q_eng. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: One discharge, field-line tracing. No actuator loop. Bare arXiv. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80. Not a ledger term.

papers.title: Parafermions in fractional Chern insulator-superconductor heterostructures: the role of spin polarization
papers.coreIdea: Designs for Z3 parafermions mostly assumed an unpolarized fractional quantum Hall edge. The fractional Chern insulators in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene look spin-polarized. In a trench between two polarized ν=2/3 edges, the pairing and tunneling terms that are still allowed are not the same ones as in the unpolarized case.
papers.whyItMatters: E-MZM is a watch item, not load-bearing. A change in which edge operators are allowed is not an independent X logical and Z logical, and it is not a measured topological gap. M5 stays open. It does not replace the S3 fusion gate set on H2.
papers.limitation: Edge theory. No device. A1 fails because E-MZM is WATCH, not KEEP or HOLD. Not a distinguisher.

papers.title: Phase Separation in Fractonic Fluids: Coarsening, Interfaces, Nucleation, and Hyperuniformity in and out of Equilibrium
papers.coreIdea: If a fluid remembers not only how much stuff is in a region but also the dipole of that stuff, droplets merge more slowly. Driving the fluid out of equilibrium quiets the interface and makes new droplets harder to start. The paper is a continuum calculation plus simulations.
papers.whyItMatters: E-FR as a hardware memory is cut. A classical fluid with extra conservation laws is not a quantum memory and not a store for a plasma snapshot. The hardware cut stands.
papers.limitation: Not a code. Not a device. Reversing the cut would take two independent C≥4 sources. This is not one of them.

papers.title: Rotation and Anisotropic Scaling in Axionic Holographic Superconductors: AdS4 versus Lifshitz5
papers.coreIdea: A holographic model of a superconductor is spun and stretched so the scaling is not the same in every direction. The question is whether condensation starts sooner in an AdS4 bulk or in a Lifshitz5 bulk. The answer is a comparison of two gravity models.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A rotating holographic superconductor is not a tokamak encoder and not a processor bus. This is the holography representative for the papers left unscored on 2 Oct. The denylist holds.
papers.limitation: Readable. Not INCLUDE. The driven holographic superfluid in the same listing stays unscored. Reversing the cut needs two independent C≥4 sources.

papers.title: Extracting Anyon Statistics from Neural Network Fractional Quantum Hall States
papers.coreIdea: Train a neural-network wavefunction for a fractional quantum Hall state, then read the modular S-matrix from entanglement interferometry. From S you get quantum dimensions, fusion rules, and braid phases.
papers.whyItMatters: A journal method for certifying that a prepared state is the anyon theory you think it is. Complements the S3 hardware demo, which certified cyclic fusion by trapping a single non-Abelian anyon on a torus.
papers.limitation: Numerical FQH, not a processor and not a plant. Journal venue can INCLUDE; still cannot raise C above 3 on the wrong platform.

papers.title: The Chern-Simons Function and the Quantum Hall Effect
papers.coreIdea: Witten walks through what is special about the Chern-Simons invariant of a gauge connection on a three-manifold and why that object sits underneath the quantum Hall effect.
papers.whyItMatters: A living foundational note, not a 1989 reprint. It is a pillar of the topology field the observatory tracks. INCLUDE as reading, not as a reactor encoding.
papers.limitation: Pedagogical field theory. Duality is not a tokamak I/O map. Must not be used to un-cut E-HOL.

papers.title: Comparing magic state cultivation methods using matrix product states
papers.coreIdea: Magic-state cultivation is how you get non-Clifford gates cheaply. The authors compare cultivation schemes with matrix product states so the space-time cost is no longer a guess.
papers.whyItMatters: Lo 2026 already prepared a topological magic state with S3 fusion. Cultivation is the competing (non-topological) route to the same resource. Bus B should know both numbers.
papers.limitation: MPS on modest sizes. Not a demonstration that cultivation beats fusion, and not a C raise for E-S3.

papers.title: Demonstration of reconstruction-free static magnetic control of DIII-D plasma with deep reinforcement learning
papers.coreIdea: An RL controller on DIII-D maps raw magnetic diagnostics straight to coils, skipping equilibrium reconstruction. Shape error stayed within 1.5–2 cm and radial position within 1 cm across L- and H-mode, including pellets and L–H transitions.
papers.whyItMatters: This is Bus A in the language of a machine that already exists: diagnostics in, actuators out, published errors versus the isoflux baseline. Journal + tokamak → Auto-Gate INCLUDE is legal. C stays C4.
papers.limitation: Static shape, not tearing avoidance, and not a quantum-in-the-loop result. Sub-millisecond VDEs remain out of scope, same caveat as PACMAN.

papers.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Plasma Control in Nuclear Fusion: Codebase and Benchmark
papers.coreIdea: RL4F is a public offline-RL benchmark for tokamak profile tracking (rotation, density, temperature, pressure) built from DIII-D historical discharges. Model-based offline RL wins on average; no single algorithm wins every task.
papers.whyItMatters: Bus A needs a named baseline. A DIII-D dataset plus closed-loop eval is exactly the attach surface M2 asked for. INCLUDE under E-RL. C already C4 from Seo / Rothstein; this does not raise it.
papers.limitation: Offline benchmark, not a disruption-avoidance shot. Dynamics are learned from history, so they inherit diagnostic coverage and do not replace a tearing-onset latency test.

papers.title: Regulation compliant AI for fusion: explainable image-based feedback control of divertor detachment in DIII-D tokamak
papers.coreIdea: An interpretable, camera-based feedback controller holds the DIII-D divertor detachment state at a requested target in real time, with about 2% mean absolute difference from target.
papers.whyItMatters: First peer-reviewed learned/interpretable control aimed at the heat-exhaust blocker. Same Bus A shape as Seo and Rothstein: diagnostics in, actuator commands out, error published against the target.
papers.limitation: Detachment control, not disruption avoidance or tearing warning. Classical controller; no quantum hardware in the loop. E-RL stays C4. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning control of quantum error correction
papers.coreIdea: Error-detection events from a running surface code double as a learning signal: a reinforcement-learning agent keeps steering the control parameters of a Willow processor during computation. Logical stability against drift improves 2.4x (3.5x with decoder steering), with a further ~20% logical-error suppression on a calibrated device.
papers.whyItMatters: Journal hardware evidence on the relevant class of machine for E-QEC, and the same 'learned agent on a classical control loop' pattern as Bus A. It does not couple the buses.
papers.limitation: E-QEC is already C4, so it cannot raise C. Abelian surface and colour codes; non-Abelian decoding is still not free. Coupling with E-RL would start at C1 and is not opened. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Efficient Preparation of Solvable Anyons with Adaptive Quantum Circuits
papers.coreIdea: Every solvable anyon theory with a gapped boundary, including non-Abelian Ising anyons, can be prepared with adaptive finite-depth circuits (local unitaries plus measurement and global classical feed-forward) by sequential gauging.
papers.whyItMatters: Journal context for how Lo 2026 prepared S3: adaptive circuits put a whole family of non-Abelian orders within reach of current processors.
papers.limitation: Theory. State preparation is not a fusion-measurement gate set; E-S3 stays C3. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Keldysh parameter for laser-nucleus interactions
papers.coreIdea: Defines a nuclear Keldysh parameter for laser-nucleus interactions; near unity the Gamow tunnelling picture fails. Near-IR (1.55 eV) WKB/Volkov estimates give a DT enhancement factor of about 90 at E0 = 10 keV and 6x10^22 W cm^-2.
papers.whyItMatters: The optimistic disputer for S-L2. Its near-IR route at 10^21-10^22 W cm^-2 sits outside the DBE-S manuscript's EUV-X-ray band, and it says the X-ray route needs about 10^23 W cm^-2.
papers.limitation: WKB/Volkov estimates that TDSE calculations (PRC 110 / PRC 112) do not reproduce. No hole burning, parametric scatter or finite-pulse penalty. S-L2 stays HOLD at C1. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Enhancing the creation of elements in laser-assisted heavy-ion fusion reactions
papers.coreIdea: Coupled-channels TDSE for laser-assisted 16O + 238U fusion: 6-60% enhancement of the sub-barrier fusion probability for quasistatic fields of 10^27-10^29 W cm^-2 with 1 eV photons. Femtosecond pulses cut this by many orders of magnitude.
papers.whyItMatters: Finite-pulse caveat for the S-L2 kill test: Vulcan-like parameters (10^23 W cm^-2, 500 fs) give about 0.05%. Same group and method as PRC 110.
papers.limitation: Heavy-ion fusion, not DT. Theory, no gain shot. Moves the ledger only in the conservative direction. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Distinguishing Majorana zero modes from trivial defect states in an iron-based superconductor
papers.coreIdea: Spin-polarized STM on Fe(Te,Se) shows that near-zero-energy states at step edges and line defects are trivial Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states, and zero-energy states away from defects cannot be attributed to Majorana bound states either.
papers.whyItMatters: A documented Majorana mimic on a second platform. Supports E-MZM WATCH and the M5 distinguisher-or-drop rule.
papers.limitation: In press: no volume or pages yet (Crossref, 2026-10-03). A negative result for one material; it does not test a nanowire X+Z logical. E-MZM stays WATCH at C1. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: The Future of Ignition
papers.coreIdea: LLNL's account of NIF after ignition: target gain 4.13 on 7 Apr 2025 (8.6 MJ from 2.08 MJ), eight ignition shots by late May 2025, burnup approaching 12%, and the Enhanced Yield Capability upgrade (2.2 to 2.6 MJ) for yields up to about 30 MJ. 100 MJ is not possible on NIF.
papers.whyItMatters: Second source for the NIF Q_sci = 4.13 baseline in the Q ledger, next to the lab shot record (nif-qsci-2025).
papers.limitation: Lab magazine, not peer-reviewed. Q_sci (target gain) is not Q_eng. S-Q stays CUT as output. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: From Ignition to Energy
papers.coreIdea: LLNL's plant-level view: a viable inertial fusion energy plant needs target gain of at least 30 (50-100 ideal) at 10-20 shots per second, with diode-pumped lasers and a closed power cycle. NIF is at gain 4.13 and about one shot a day.
papers.whyItMatters: Sources plant gain and repetition rate for the ICF side of the Q ledger (M1). It narrows, but does not close, the driver-efficiency marker.
papers.limitation: Lab magazine. No driver wall-plug efficiency number and no recirculating-power breakdown. Q = 1000 stays a ledger stress test. Queued, not applied: triage proposes ADD (citation), so the catalog shows HOLD until a review card INCLUDEs it. No version bump.

papers.title: Quantum State of a Gravitating Spacetime Region
papers.coreIdea: Associates a gravitational Hilbert space and quantum states with compact spatial regions using the gravitational path integral; when one saddle dominates, the state has a classical Lorentzian spacetime interpretation.
papers.whyItMatters: Holography and quantum gravity stay on the reading list. Duality is not a tokamak I/O map.
papers.limitation: CUT (lab rule): binds the E-HOL denylist. Reading is allowed; INCLUDE is not. Triage READING-LIST: kept in the library on the reading list, cut from the engine.

papers.title: Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator
papers.coreIdea: Circularly polarized femtosecond pulses at 1,550 nm turn monolayer graphene into a Floquet topological insulator; a phase-locked second harmonic then steers electrons in the light-dressed bands (photocurrent circular dichroism, an all-optical anomalous Hall effect, valley-polarized currents).
papers.whyItMatters: Floquet physics stays on the reading list. This is driven topology in a real material, not a system clock.
papers.limitation: Femtosecond light-dressed states, not a prethermal lifetime against a control horizon. E-TC stays CUT as metronome. Triage READING-LIST: kept in the library on the reading list, cut from the engine.

papers.title: Bayesian Active Learning of Ion Loss-Cone Boundaries in Tokamaks
papers.coreIdea: A tokamak loss-cone boundary is learned instead of being filled in by brute force. A Bayesian logistic model spends a fixed budget of guiding-center orbits, then stores a loss probability and its uncertainty on a mesh of launch points.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL is plant attach. This is an orbit-loss database, not a coil command and not a disruption shot. M2 stays open. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. One analytic equilibrium. Harvest confidence is a preprint gauge, not C.

papers.title: Resonant and Ponderomotive Pumping of Zonal Flows by Turbulence, Alfvén Eigenmodes, and Radiofrequency Waves
papers.coreIdea: Zonal flows can be pumped by drift-wave turbulence, Alfvén eigenmodes, or radiofrequency waves. The drive is a short formula in the wave's canonical momentum and the power it dissipates, covering the ponderomotive push and quasilinear diffusion.
papers.whyItMatters: S-L3 keeps Vlasov, hole-burning, and SRS-SBS inside the rate. This formula does not replace those solvers and it does not write a reactivity. C stays at C4. It is not an E-RL attach, so no bridge is opened.
papers.limitation: Analytic preprint. Not a Vlasov run and not a laser-plasma scatter shot. Q_eng is not an output.

papers.title: Classical simulation of coherent crosstalk in surface codes
papers.coreIdea: Nearest-neighbor ZZ crosstalk on a surface-code state has a syndrome distribution a classical computer can sample in polynomial time. Add coherent single-qubit noise as well and that efficient sampling disappears unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is the error layer. A limit on simulating coherent crosstalk is not a measured memory and does not move the hardware threshold. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. Complexity, not a device. No new hardware threshold.

papers.title: From Random Quantum Codes to Explicit qLDPC Codes via Local Properties
papers.coreIdea: Random codes have parameters that explicit codes rarely match, and a quantum code is asked to be LDPC as well. This paper gives nested CSS spaces a local-witness language and, from it, explicit qLDPC constructions for quantum list decoding and list recovery.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC wants explicit qLDPC, not only random existence. A rate-threshold theorem and a list-decoding construction are not a memory experiment and do not tighten the C4 hardware bound. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv, primary category cs.IT. No physical-error threshold and no named code distance in the abstract. No device.

papers.title: Self-testing the toric code against classical communication
papers.coreIdea: The toric-code space, spread over a network shaped like a torus, can be self-tested from correlations alone. The honest parties never talk. The certificate still holds if the devices secretly exchange classical messages out to a distance that grows with the network.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC's evidence is a memory that runs, not a device-independent certificate. Self-testing the code space does not replace a threshold shot. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No processor and no decoder benchmark.

papers.title: Layer codes as quantum memories: syndrome extraction, thresholds and idle robustness
papers.coreIdea: Layer codes are three-dimensional local CSS codes with check weight at most six, made by quasi-concatenating an input code with surface-code patches. This paper builds the syndrome circuits, including the junctions a borrowed surface-code schedule cannot handle, and compares eighteen of them with surface codes of the same distance under circuit-level noise.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC is where a memory either holds or it does not. The [[4,2,2]] family reaches a simulated circuit-level threshold of 5.06(7)e-3 and idles longer than a rotated surface code of the same distance, at the cost of more operations and about five times as many physical qubits per logical qubit. That is a simulation, not a below-threshold hardware run. C stays at C4. Importance 88 is still a harvest gauge.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. The threshold and the idle-time factors are circuit simulations at fixed distance, not a device, and not a license to scale one parameter without bound. Harvest confidence 74 is under 80.

papers.title: Graph Neural Post-selection for Quantum Error Correction
papers.coreIdea: A graph net looks at the syndrome, and at belief-propagation posteriors for high-rate qLDPC codes, and rejects shots that look like logical failures, without running the decoder again.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC may use post-selection as a tool. These factors are simulations under circuit-level depolarizing noise. They do not raise C. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. The gain is at one keep-rate and one noise model. Not a hardware shot.

papers.title: Rapid Vacuum Response Calculations for Non-axisymmetric Plasma Geometries
papers.coreIdea: Free-boundary ideal MHD needs the magnetic energy in the vacuum outside the plasma. This paper computes that response, and the surface inductance, for non-axisymmetric walls, fast enough for on the order of 10^5 boundary points on a laptop.
papers.whyItMatters: E-RL attaches commands to a plant. A vacuum matrix is an input to three-dimensional stability, not a coil command. M2 stays open. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No plasma shot and no disruption metric. License is CC BY 4.0; the PDF is not committed.

papers.title: Composite fermions in ideal Chern bands
papers.coreIdea: Composite fermions turn a fractional quantum Hall fluid into an integer state in a weaker field. This paper asks what changes when the uniform field is replaced by the uneven Berry curvature of a Chern band, and it writes Jain states and their quasiparticles for Aharonov-Casher bands.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 needs non-Abelian braid plus a fusion measurement. These are composite-fermion quasiparticles in an ideal Chern band. An isolated quasiparticle band whose Berry flux differs from a Landau level is not an S3 fusion space and not a braid on hardware. Fusion measurement stays in the gate set. C stays at C3. No new bus.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. No device. The abstract's claim about an isolated quasiparticle is not turned into a gate.

papers.title: A Code-Agnostic Graph Neural Network Decoder from the Detection Error Model
papers.coreIdea: POLYMECHANON is a graph-net decoder whose only input is the detection error model of a code: detectors, error mechanisms, and logical observables. The same architecture is meant to decode any stabilizer code once that graph is known.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC's C4 is a measured memory, not a better simulated decoder. Up to 25% fewer logical failures than correlated matching on the rotated surface code, and up to 16% fewer on [[130,4,6]], does not raise C. It is not an S3 decoder. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv, CC BY 4.0. The [[130,4,6]] comparison is a simulation. The same abstract says a model trained across families tends to fail on unseen codes, especially larger ones. No hardware.

papers.title: From Modal Memory to Topological Relaxation in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
papers.coreIdea: A driven holographic superfluid is brought to the same present drive by different histories, then run on the same future protocol. The histories end in the same winding sector, but the time spent in the previous sector changes by about a factor of 3.7, organized by a modal imbalance.
papers.whyItMatters: E-HOL is cut. A holographic superfluid is not a tokamak encoder and not a processor bus. The rest of that holography cluster stays unscored. The denylist holds.
papers.limitation: Readable. Not INCLUDE. Reversal is not requested.

papers.title: Learned Parallel Bit-Flipping Sequential Belief Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.coreIdea: Belief propagation on qLDPC codes often fails to settle, because of short cycles and degeneracy. This paper learns an update order, then, if the syndrome is still wrong, tries several Pauli flips and continues those tries in parallel.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC needs fast decoders. A learned schedule is still a preprint method, not a change to C4. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. License is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so the PDF is not mirrored. The abstract text used here does not quote a logical-error rate, and none is added.

papers.title: Generalized Effective Spin-Chain formalism for multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
papers.coreIdea: Strongly interacting multicomponent anyons in a one-dimensional optical lattice are mapped to a spin chain. The charge motion becomes spinless fermions. The statistical phase shows up in the spin exchange, not in the leading charge Hamiltonian. Out of equilibrium, successive exchanges pick up a direction-dependent phase.
papers.whyItMatters: E-S3 is braid plus fusion for a topological qubit, not a one-dimensional exchange phase. This does not replace fusion measurement. C stays at C3. It was left unscored on 30 Sep.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv. One-dimensional lattice. No braid experiment and no fusion readout.

papers.title: Logical information localisation in stabiliser codes via single-qubit measurements
papers.coreIdea: When a stabilizer code loses qubits, stabiliser path finding tries to park the logical information on one chosen qubit using a single round of single-qubit measurements. This paper lets the target be any set of at most g qubits, and proves that random loss below one half still localises on a large enough planar surface code.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC cares about loss. The C4 evidence is a running memory. A localisation threshold does not raise C. The abstract's 'logical fusion' is a stabilizer communication step, not an S3 fusion measurement, so no bridge is opened. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv, CC BY 4.0. The proof is for planar surface codes. Not a qLDPC hardware result.

papers.title: Entropy threshold: A simple proxy for performance of quantum error correction
papers.coreIdea: Thresholds of error-correcting protocols are expensive to simulate. This paper estimates them by comparing the entropy of the noise with the information gained from stabilizer measurements, spacetime detectors, or flag qubits.
papers.whyItMatters: E-QEC already has a measured surface-code threshold. A back-of-the-envelope proxy does not replace that shot and does not tighten C. C stays at C4.
papers.limitation: Bare arXiv, CC BY 4.0. The abstract says the proxy tracks numerical thresholds. It does not quote a threshold value in the text used here, so none is entered.

papers.title: ARC: A compact, high-field, fusion nuclear science facility and demonstration power plant with demountable magnets
papers.coreIdea: MIT's ARC conceptual design is a compact, high-field HTS tokamak with demountable magnets. Its design point is 525 MW of fusion power, 708 MW of total thermal power, a plant thermal efficiency of 0.40, 283 MW of total electric and 190 MW of net electric output, so Q_e = 3.0. The lower-hybrid chain draws 69.6 MW from the wall to launch 25.0 MW.
papers.whyItMatters: Second, independent anchor for the MCF recirculating-power term of the Q ledger: P_recirc = 283 − 190 = 93 MW, f_recirc ≈ 1/3. Even the 'aggressive Pilot' case (Brayton ~50%, 261 MW net, Q_e = 3.8) is about 260 times above the f_recirc = 1e-3 that Q_eng = 1000 needs.
papers.limitation: Conceptual design, not a built plant. The authors say Q_e is a Brayton estimate for the fusion power core alone and the whole-plant Q_e is lower. Tokamak, not stellarator. Binds S-Q, which is CUT as an output, so it can never be an ADD; ledger input only. No version bump.

papers.title: Diode laser pumps for future inertial fusion energy systems: status and perspectives
papers.coreIdea: A status review of diode-laser pumps for diode-pumped solid-state IFE drivers. It restates the beamline wall-plug efficiency requirement, including cooling, as at least 10% at a repetition rate of at least 10 Hz, and notes that a first IFE DPSSL demonstration may run at a relaxed 7%. Diode electrical-to-optical efficiency of at least 70% is a separate, component-level number.
